contribution.position: My position on reliability is unchanged. The perf report records p99 latency of 410ms at peak load against a 250ms budget, and the incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms. Over-budget latency is the condition that tends to trigger client timeouts and retries, so the measurement matches a failure mode already seen in production. The QA turn cites the same perf report for a 180ms p99, but the artifact text says 410ms. That discrepancy needs reconciling before the risk axis can lean on it. The passing tests (412 passed, 0 failed) are functional results and say nothing about peak-load behavior. Evidence still needed: (a) whether the 410ms comes from the changed code path or from the test environment, (b) the client retry and backoff configuration and whether it stays bounded at that latency, and (c) a repeat load test with p99 inside budget, or a documented and approved exception.
